audit.why: 54.35% Emerald+ over 804 games supports the Vex-favoured chart.
Even-to-favoured lane vs an immobile scaling mage; the danger is his root-into-EQ chain and his scaling, both covered.
Spikes (early poke edge, 6 vs immobility, first-item window, deny-his-scaling late) are coherent and specific.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] calls Rune Prison 'slow-cast' — it is instant point-and-click at 615 range; and the page never says the root only happens on a Flux-marked target (otherwise it is just a slow), which is the actual dodge-window fact of the lane.
audit.why: Riot text: 'If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.'
audit.corrected: spikes[1] rewritten; Flux condition and W 11-9s added to cooldowns.

audit.why: W 11-9s, Q 5s, E 3.5-2.5s from the kit.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Personal Space has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Rune Prison is 11-9s and only ROOTS if Spell Flux marked you first — the E throw is your two-second warning to back off. - His Q resets every 5s off other casts; never stand still in the 1000-range line. - Your W has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: E-mark the contact, Q through the marked line for the fear, auto, walk — every trade he answers with a dash just schedules the next fear.
edits.after: Your Q travels 1200 and his whole kit answers at 615 — fire the feared bolt from the range band where his only reply is spending mana on a wave.

edits.before: Spending the W pulse on poke spacing and then eating the real engage unfeared — the pulse is the matchup against everything that moves fast.
edits.after: Once Spell Flux tags you his W becomes a root and the EQ chain follows — poking inside 615 with the debuff ticking is how even lanes end in his favour.

edits.before: Your R (Shadow Surge) is a clean answer to an immobile target: he has only Flash and his slow-cast W root to avoid your all-in. If he burns W to root you, respect it, but once it's down you can R-in, W, and E-fear-combo him with no escape. He can't dodge your ult the way a mobile mid could.
edits.after: Your R (Shadow Surge) is a clean answer to an immobile target: he has only Flash and his W to stop your all-in, and W only roots if his Spell Flux marked you first. Once W is down — an 11-9s window — you can R-in, shield, and E-fear-combo him with no escape. He can't dodge your ult the way a mobile mid could.

notes: Chart aligned: phases[3..6].side moved to Vex, side-only — win[3..6], the packet levelChart and the content whys all already said Vex; the full layer's Ryze verdict on first-item/late rows contradicted every other source. Ryze's famous late scaling is represented in the prose as the thing you deny, which is consistent with a Vex-favoured late row at this win rate; if the user prefers Ryze-late rows here, phases[5..6] plus win[5..6] plus whys[5..6] must all flip together. Added the Flux-then-root mechanic (W only roots on a Flux-marked target) — the single most actionable fact in the lane. No misgendering (Ryze is he/him).
